title: Buca Chicken Marsala
blurb: The bacon fat left in the pan becomes the base for the Marsala sauce, so the bacon seasons the whole dish instead of just garnishing it.
steps: Coat a large skillet lightly with olive oil and set over medium-high heat. Add the bacon and cook until crisp and lightly browned. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving the fat in the pan.
Put the flour on a plate. Pat the cutlets dry, season lightly with salt and pepper, then dredge in the flour.

Heat the pan with the bacon fat over medium-high heat, adding a touch more olive oil if needed to make about 2 tablespoons. When hot, shake the excess flour off the cutlets and add them to the pan. Sauté, turning once, until browned on both sides — thin cutlets only need a few minutes per side. Remove the cutlets and pour off the excess fat.
With the pan still over medium-high heat, add the Marsala and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom. Cook until reduced by about a quarter.
Stir in the cream and simmer until nicely thickened. Return the chicken and bacon to the pan, turning to coat, and reheat a minute.
Serve with the sauce spooned over the top and a sprinkling of parsley.
